newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 ends bearish week with sharp losses.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 ends bearish week with sharp losses.

text.p: The Czech PX50 suffered its biggest fall of the week on Friday as the sustained downtrend affecting major issues gathered pace.
The three largest issues on the exchange -- SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- fell on average by nearly three percent.
Analysts said there was still room for further falls but predicted relatively stronger support for Komercni Banka.
"I think now there are some investors, particularly in Komercni Banka, interested in getting back into that stock," said John Vax of ING Barings.
The broader market was equally bearish.

Computer systems company PVT was the biggest decliner falling 155 crowns to 2,945. On Friday PVT said it posted a 1996 net loss of 15.9 million crowns compared with a profit of 532 million crowns in 1995.
Conference oraginser BVV Brno lost 100 crowns to 3,200.
Friday's losses concluded a bad week for Czech equities. The PX50 declined over the period by 3.5 percent.
